messages:
emma_sales: Quick sync: Client wants Private POC. They can do either VPC Peering or AWS PrivateLink. Ops wants pros/cons + exact steps they hand to cloud team.
ryan_solns: TL;DR: PrivateLink = fewer route changes & cross-account isolation. Peering = direct routing & slightly lower latency but needs route/security updates.
jess_net: If they pick peering we need: their account id, vpc id, list of route table ids for subnets they want reachable, and confirm non-overlapping CIDRs.
sasha_sre: Security needs: mTLS enforced at app layer (we terminate TLS on our side), KMS CMK policy to allow cross-account decrypt for logs if they request S3, and an audit retention plan.
client_ops: We prefer peering because we already route via our inspection VPC. Firewall sits in 10.100.0.0/16 and app VPC is 10.20.0.0/16.
jess_net: Confirmed: peering path requires adding routes in both VPC route tables: example CLI commands below. Make sure their inspection VPC has route to the peer too.

# CLI example for peering (awscli)
aws ec2 create-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-id vpc-0client --peer-vpc-id vpc-0redwood --peer-owner-id 123456789012
aws ec2 accept-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0xxxxxx
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0clientpublic --destination-cidr-block 10.200.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0xxxxxx
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0redwood --destination-cidr-block 10.20.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0xxxxxx

sasha_sre: For PrivateLink, we will create a VPC Endpoint Service in our account and provide the service name. They create an interface endpoint in chosen subnets with security group allowing outbound 443. Sample Terraform snippet below.

# Terraform snippet (interface endpoint)
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_api" {
  vpc_id            = var.client_vpc_id
  service_name      = "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-abcdefgh"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = var.client_subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [var.allowed_sg]
  private_dns_enabled = true
}

infrobot: Note: creating endpoint service will require us to add allowed principals if they want cross-account. Also POC API key issuance will check quotas. Open ticket if limits hit.
ryan_solns: Actionable checklist for client ops to unblock POC:
- Choose connectivity: PEERING or PRIVATELINK
- Provide: account-id, vpc-id, subnet-ids, route-table-ids, CIDR blocks (check overlap)
- Provide firewall/transit gateway details if traffic must flow via inspection
- Confirm whether logs should be pushed to their S3 (provide bucket ARN)
- Designate a technical contact for direct ops call

emma_sales: On our side we'll provide:
- Temporary limited API key scoped to the POC (valid 14 days)
- Private endpoint service name (if PL chosen) or peering accept config + route commands
- KMS policy snippet for cross-account decrypt (if S3 logging)

sasha_sre: KMS policy example (give to their security team):
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{ "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::CLIENT_ACCOUNT:root"}, "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"], "Resource": "*" }]}

client_ops: Ops review scheduled tomorrow. Can you send the PL service-name and the peering template? Also need pin instructions for the model build we deploy.
ryan_solns: Will send both templates + a short model pinning command (API param: model_version=redwood-inference/v1.2.3). Also mention expected egress endpoints (control plane for metrics: metrics.redwood.ai:443).
emma_sales: I'll drop a consolidated doc in this thread and ping when done. If they want a Zoom handoff, set time and include jess and sasha.
infrobot: Reminder: creating POC in prod requires JIRA ticket #POC-XXXX for audit.
ryan_solns: One final note: if they insist on peering and have Transit Gateway, we support peering via TGW but need the TGW id and attachment ids.
client_ops: Thanks all. We'll reply with the requested fields by EOD.
